facts.value: Operating systems are the layer of software that manages a computer's resources for its users and their applications.

1. Allocating resources between different applications, deciding when they will receive CPU time or space in memory. 2. Providing an interface that abstracts the details of accessing hardware details to make things easier for programmers. 3. Offering common services, such as an interface for accessing network and disk devices, allowing applications to run on different hardware without needing to be rewritten.
Application software runs on top of the operating system and uses the computer's resources to perform a task.
Traditional applications are purchased with a perpetual license for a specific version of the software, downloaded, and run on hardware belonging to the purchaser.
Software as a service (SaaS) is a model in which the provider hosts the software and provides the use of the software to customers, often in exchange for a subscription fee.
By 2023, SaaS products had become the primary method that companies deliver applications, usually delivered via a web application.
Programming languages are the format in which software is written.
Since the 1950s, thousands of different programming languages have been invented; some have been in use for decades, while others have fallen into disuse.
Some definitions classify machine code and assembly language as programming languages.
Programs written in high-level programming languages must be both human-readable and capable of being translated into unambiguous instructions for computer hardware.
Knowledge of machine code is not necessary to write high-level programming languages.
High-level programming languages can be ported to other computer systems.
High-level programming languages are more concise and human-readable than machine code.
The invention of high-level programming languages was simultaneous with compilers needed to translate them automatically into machine code.

facts.value: Since the mid-1970s, software and its source code have been protected by copyright law that vests the owner with the exclusive right to copy the code.
The underlying ideas or algorithms are not protected by copyright law, but are sometimes treated as a trade secret and concealed by such methods as non-disclosure agreements.
A software copyright is often owned by the person or company that financed or made the software (depending on their contracts with employees or contractors who helped to write it).
Some software is in the public domain and has no restrictions on who can use it, copy or share it, or modify it; a notable example is software written by the United States Government.
Free and open-source software also allow free use, sharing, and modification, perhaps with a few specified conditions.
The use of some software is governed by an agreement (software license) written by the copyright holder and imposed on the user.
